_about: Control-scheme step 3 (ADR 0008; control-rules.md sections 1, 2 and 6): the costs, cooldowns and windows of what a fighter does inside an exchange, read by sim/director/interrupt.gd (DirInterrupt). Game Design's numbers. Ticks are sim ticks (60 a second); ki is out of 100. The perfect block's lockout and assist factor are Controls' (data/input/timing.json perfectBlock), and its stagger and riposte lengths are Combat's (templates.json profiles.dynamic.perfectBlock).

perfectBlock._note: ki: gained by the blocker. stopTicks: the hit-stop on the block. windows: the last ticks of the wind-up in which a fresh guard press is a perfect block, by strike class (moveset-rules.md section 11(f)); an opener and a blast depend on the exchange's weight; a class not listed has no window. early: ticks before the window opens in which a press still counts, by class. oneArmedOff: ticks off every window for a blocker with a broken arm. The lockout and the assist factor are Controls' (data/input/timing.json perfectBlock antiMashLockout, assistFactor). Touch's 2 extra ticks need the slot's layout in the sim and are not applied yet. blow: a brawl's light or flurry blow (it is announced only light.contactTicks ahead, so the press is a read of the flurry's rhythm)

dodgeCancel._note: ki and cooldownTicks: control-rules.md section 2 (15 ki, 3 s). gapTicks: the defender may cancel only this long after it was last struck (a gap between strikes, never hit-stun). dash: the speed of the dash in the held direction, units a second. freeBeforeWindup: the attacker's cancel costs nothing until his first wind-up starts (agency-pass.md section 1, solution E); it then starts freeGapTicks of cooldown and not cooldownTicks

burst._note: ki and cooldownTicks: 30 ki, 8 s. rangeBh: a rival within this many body heights is shoved. pushSpeed: the shove, units a second (about 8 bh of travel). baitStaggerTicks: the burster's stagger when the rival was guarding. threatTicks: a fighter struck within this long is 'being hit', so a power press bursts at once. autoLink: the chain link at which a Simple-layout slot (autoBurst) bursts when it pressed nothing

reversal._note: ki, or kiPatient after patientTicks of continuous guard (20, or 10 after 2 s); cooldownTicks 6 s. afterBlockTicks: how long after a normal block the press works. delayTicks: the turn before the defender's own heavy starts. landTicks: how long after the turn that heavy may still start at once

blockedString._note: a string blocked to its end leaves the attacker unable to act for this long, and the guard may start an attack at once in that time (control-rules.md section 6, point 3)

stale._note: the same weight, mode and direction in 'after' exchanges running: each further repeat adds windupPerRepeat ticks to its wind-ups (at most windupMax) and windowPerRepeat ticks to the rival's perfect-block window (at most windowMax). A change of weight, mode or direction clears it

arrival._note: The attacker's arrival side: with the stick up or down past tiltDead as he presses, his approach passes over (or under) the rival and lands on the far side. riseBh: how far over, in body heights. overShare: the share of the approach spent reaching the point above him

return._note: The return from a send (Orb, 2026-10-15). A fighter free again after a launch, a knock-back or a fall is returning for forTicks at most, until his first blow back. His approach back lasts minTicks at least and crouches windTicks before it moves; his first blow back lands firstWindTicks later than it would, with a windup cue (text return). A press of his rival on that approach, past the crouch and meetMinTicks or more before he arrives, meets it in the middle.

bands._note: The ranged press (agency-pass.md section 1; sim/director/bands.gd). The bands are measured centre to centre, the shortest arc and the height together, in body heights (75 u): close within closeBh, mid to midBh, far beyond. A close press starts its exchange at once. A press from farther off starts only the attacker's approach: it ends engageBh from the rival, on the attacker's own side and at the rival's height, and the exchange is planned then (the wind-up follows). The rival is free until it ends. lunge (the mid band) and far.light, far.heavy (the far band, by the press's weight): the approach lasts the distance to cover at 'speed' (units a second), in whole ticks, at least minTicks and at most maxTicks. Until the far taunt and the held charge are built a far press flies in on a tap, at about the speed it had (4000 u a second; it was 2600 with the wind-up inside the flight); the charge's own flight (light 0.5 to 1.5 s, heavy 0.8 to 2.0 s) comes with the hold. On a slope the end point is brought in until the pair is inside the close band
bands._edge: midBh is 12.5 (agency-pass.md section 12 b): a match opens with the pair 12 bh apart, and the opening press is a lunge. hysteresisBh: the band is held state, and an edge is crossed only half this much beyond it (going out it sits further out, coming in further in), so the band and its icon do not flicker for a pair hovering on a line
bands._far: The far band (agency-pass.md section 1). taunt: a tap is a taunt, a challenge that plays for windowTicks while he keeps flying; the rival's attack press in that time answers it and both rush to the middle (meet: each covers half the distance at 'speed', in whole ticks between minTicks and maxTicks, and they arrive together, engageBh apart; chargerEdge: a rival met while he held a heavy charge enters the clash with this many points (of 100) off the attacker's chance, the interim form of Game Design's +5 until the fist clash on the pulse is wired). Answered, it pays in full; ignored, a half, a quarter, an eighth, then nothing until the two have traded blows. charge: a press still held holdTicks after it becomes a charge of that weight, flying at 'speed' for minTicks to maxTicks (section 12 a: a light goes after 8 ticks and flies 0.3 to 1.0 s; a heavy after 16 and flies 0.5 to 1.4 s). A light charge stops for nothing when the button is let go; a heavy charge is committed (only a dodge-cancel at its full cost stops it) and its heavy counts as held, so landing it earns a launch. taunt.enabled false: a far press flies in on a tap at far.light or far.heavy, as before

blast._note: Energy, the first slice (agency-pass.md section 5 and section 11, item 6; sim/director/blast.gd). With the energy family held, an attack press outside an exchange fires a blast from where he stands, in any band. light: a bolt (the kind in data/fight/shots.json) for 'ki', leaving windupTicks after the press (a light still held waits for its release, up to holdTicks, so a layout's hold can turn it into the heavy); presses while one winds up queue up to queueMax more; bolts fired within groupTicks of each other are one volley; the AI's light is aiVolley bolts. heavy: a charged shot for 'ki'; it charges while the button is held and leaves when it is let go (not before windupTicks, and by itself at holdMaxTicks); its damage rises from tapShare of the kind's to all of it over chargeTicks. stopTicks: the hit-stop of a blast that lands. charge: a fighter in a heavy charge takes a shot of power up to shrugPower at shrugMul of its damage and keeps coming; a stronger shot, or any shot on a light charge, stops him. The perfect block's window is perfectBlock.windows.blast; the shot's speed, power and damage are the kind's

barrage._note: A barrage closes (agency-pass.md sections 16 and 21). When enderAfter of a fighter's shots, of any kind, land clean on his rival inside 'window' ticks (not guarded, not shrugged off, not deflected; each shot once, and the shots of a split or a rain once for their group), the last is a knock-back he did not press: decisive (kind barrage), never a launch. measuredTicks: if each was fired this many ticks or more after the one before, it goes enderDist.measured of the tier's knock-back distance and is a full set-up; otherwise enderDist.plain and launch.json setup.weight.barragePlain. immune: the count starts again and the rival cannot be knocked back by another barrage for this many ticks. tappedHeavyWeak (section 22): a barrage that includes a tapped, uncharged heavy shot gets the weak ender, as a spammed one does

deflect._note: Deflects (agency-pass.md section 15.2). Where a deflected shot goes is the core's (data/fight/shots.json deflect: wild with scatter on, back at the shooter with it off). freeApproachTicks: a perfect block of a shot gives him this long to start a charge or a lunge that no shot stops (a shot that meets him on it is shrugged off at charge.shrugMul); 0 switches it off. context.ki: with guard held, the context press sets a deflect on the shot coming at him for this much ki, with no timing; it sends the shot off with none of the perfect block's rewards

spray._note: The spray cone (agency-pass.md section 15.4). A bolt fired measuredTicks or more after his last seeks, and his spread recovers by recoverPerSec a second. Each bolt fired sooner adds perBolt to his spread, up to max. A bolt then still seeks with a chance of 1 - missShare x spread; otherwise it flies straight inside the cone at the rival, a half-angle whose slope runs from slopeMin (6 degrees) at no spread to slopeMax (18 degrees) at full, and explodes where it lands. light.aiGapTicks: the AI spaces the bolts of its volley this many ticks apart, so its bolts are measured and keep seeking

mine._note: Mines (agency-pass.md sections 15.5 and 17). With the energy family held, the context press lays a mine of 'kind' (data/fight/shots.json) where he is for 'ki': on the ground when his feet are within groundWithinBh of it, else hovering. Within shoveWithinBh of the rival the press is the energy shove's (not built: nothing). blowR: a landed blow whose target's chest is within this of a mine sets it off. The cap, the gap, the arming, the trigger, the blast, the chain and the fuse are the kind's own. A mine's blast on the rival cannot be dodged or deflected; unguarded it knocks him back from the mine and is decisive

pace._note: Pacing between exchanges (sim/director/exchange.gd cooldownAfter). cooldown: the seconds after an exchange before the next may start: min, plus perSec for each second the exchange ran, at most max. bands.lunge.windupTicks (melee-press-feel.md section 2b): a mid-band lunge holds its crouch this many ticks before it moves, by the press's weight

signature._note: Game Design's provisional signature limit (agency-pass.md section 5; Orb's to revisit once he has played the energy slice). provisional true: a signature recharges in cooldownSec and does damageMul of its damage; it still costs 45 ki. false: the fighter's own sigCooldown (120 s) and full damage, as before. QA's band to watch: signatures deal at most 30% of a match's damage

buried._note: The buried fighter (agency-pass.md sections 7 and 14.5; sim/director/bury.gd; World's embed holds him down for its own ticks, data/biomes/contact.json embed.ticks). followTicks: his rival's first attack press this soon after the burial is the free follow-up. A physical press is a dive: the director flies him to the crater at dive.speed (units a second, the light charge's; at least dive.minTicks), and the blow must land by landByTick of the burial, otherwise there is no follow-up. It is one heavy blow of 'damage' that he cannot answer, free of ki, with no launch, and it makes his crater 'deepen' times as deep as it was (WorldCrater.deepen). An energy press is the other free blow: a charged shot of blast.damage, free of ki, that arrives from any distance (data/fight/shots.json arriveTicks). He is held until the blow lands, never past landByTick; nothing of his stops a follow-up on its way. One follow-up to a burial. guardFromTick: his guard counts from this tick, or once the follow-up is used. burstFromTick: his burst throws him out, not before this tick; an AI bursts only when no follow-up is coming, with its rival within burstWithinBh (ai.json buriedBurst). safeTicks: out of the crater he is safe this long: no exchange starts on him and a shot passes

beamPlays._note: The beam plays (agency-pass.md section 5; rule-of-cool.md section 2; sim/director/beamplay.gd). enabled false: a beam is decided at its fire beat, as before. travelTicks: a signature not answered in its tell reaches the defender this many ticks after it fires, at any distance; the outcome is read on that tick. afterTicks: the exchange's length after that. dodge: a dodge tap in the last beforeTicks of the tell or the first afterTicks of the beam avoids it, with no roll. late: the defender's own signature or heavy energy attack within ticks of the fire stops the beam in a struggle that starts scoreAdd on his score. The perfect block's window against a beam is perfectBlock.windows.beam; its look is the direction held as the beam reaches him: away the swat, level the split, toward the walk. A held guard with the stick toward is the wade (guard damage, no launch). walk: he advances at speed (units a second), for minTicks to maxTicks, and the attacker is left recoverTicks of recovery when he arrives. split: two lesser beams leave him spreadDeg either side of the beam's line, lenBh long, at widthMul of its width and powerMul of its power. swat: the turned beam is lenBh long; a fighter with an anguish meter sends it up at skyDeg, one with a menace meter at the nearest standing building within lenBh, anyone else down at groundDeg

anywhere._note: Launch anywhere, Game Design's thirteenth round (docs/design/launch-anywhere.md) as re-ruled in ff68e994, behind enabled (false: window 1's launcher, its rest and its hammer, read from the keys above). link: B within this many ticks of one of his clean landed blows is the launcher; kept: a B pressed this many ticks or fewer before one lands is held and thrown as the launcher; mashTicks: a B within this of his last B is the heavy flurry. power: string by his run (1 to 4 points) x state (sure, hard, answerable) x timing (perfect, chain, max: waiting on the perfect window) x wounds (the region the piece strikes); it scales the launching blow's worth and the send. fresh: each launch marks its kind on the fighter it sends; x factor for each mark of the kind and x general for each mark of any kind within windowS, never under floor; the planner takes preferW off a candidate for each mark of its kind (the brake's air sense is Simulation's, data/fight/brake.json). aim.bendCos: the most the choreographer bends a send inside the stick's kind (the cosine of 30 degrees). full: a launch whose power at the send is this or more is full (QA's counter; the cue launch_power). The launcher is armoured against lights (an answerable one takes one light, and a second in its wind-up stops it: 2026-10-18; armourLightTicks: only if it lands within this many live ticks of the first, and a later one is the new first, so only a real flurry stops it: 2026-10-19, 5a), and only a sure one holds his stagger. fresh.destruction false: freshness never lowers the power World's building ladder reads (Orb, homework 30). aiAim: the AI's launcher aim by its personality, up, across and down weights for the hero (care above 0, or the hero role at care 0; across less where people are popAtBh body heights along the line, within popR) and the Anti-hero (care below 0, or a villain or rival role).

pop._note: Game Design's rulings-2026-10-23c: a launcher under full (after freshness) pops him bh up and back down in reach over ticks; the brawl holds; tech in the last techTicks with a dodge tap, else he reels landReel; a light after burstAfter bursts him out (down in fallTicks); a second pop in a row lands him; a pop counts stringPoints toward the next launcher. With it, no string armour (hardFromChain is not read). false: every launcher sends, as before

brawl._note: The brawl, slice B1 (sim/director/brawl.gd; docs/design/melee-press-feel.md sections 1 to 3, 5 to 7). enabled: in the close band a light or a heavy against a rival who stands or guards starts a brawl, where each fighter has his own strike line and every press is a blow; false, every exchange is planned from its template as before. interrupts: the takeovers a brawl allows (the dodge-cancel and the burst always apply). breakBh: past this many body heights apart the brawl lets go. pullBhPerSec: drift is pulled back to striking distance (templates.json contact.offset) and to one height at up to this speed. idleTicks: with no attack from either for this long it ends. heldPressTicks: a press he cannot throw at once is held this long (the latest only). stringLapseTicks: his string is over when no blow of his was thrown or landed for this long. recoil: the push of a blow, units a second (a blow leans him and does not move him). tradeTicks: two light blows that land within this of each other are a trade: both land, their beats carry trade and tradeWith (the other's piece), and a trade cue goes out. damageMul: what a brawl light is worth against the data's light (Game Design, melee-press-feel.md section 9b): the stream, lights and flurry blows, takes it in full; it is QA's lever for match length, and the ratios below are the rule. heavyMul: a heavy and an ender are worth the data's heavy times the scale times this. skillMul and setMul: a skill strike and a set light, in brawl lights (B2 and later; skillMul also sets what an answering blow outside a brawl is worth). With the brawl on, a blow outside a brawl is worth its form too (DirBrawl.worth): a light-class blow the scale, a heavy-class blow the scale times heavyMul, a chain link's blow one brawl light, and the first damaging blow of a riposte with a light, of a dodge template and of a light charge's arrival a skill strike; a heavy charge's arrival is a heavy held to full; signatures, finishers and the blow on a buried rival keep their damage. aiPerfectEveryTicks: the AI weighs a perfect block against a light at most once in this long (a fresh guard press cannot be mashed), and against every heavy. aiReversalEveryTicks: it weighs a reversal on a block at most once in this long. light: damage, the ticks from press to contact, a lone light's length, and `recover`: after a light his line is free for a heavy this long after its contact. flurry: lights tapped minGap to maxGap ticks apart are a flurry; a blow lasts one tap gap and does mul of a light by its gap ([gap, share] points, straight lines between: the interval over 10, so damage a second is level from 5 to 10 taps); a landed blow reels the rival reelTicks. The run (melee-press-feel.md section 3): each fighter's run goes up one for each light or flurry blow he lands and down replyTakes, never below 0, for each that lands on him; a heavy on him clears it, and so do runLapseTicks without landing; a blocked blow changes nothing. At a run of runToClose his next landed light is the close: it staggers the rival staggerTicks in place, decisive at launch.json setup.weight.blurPlain of a set-up. A trade is on while both have landed a light inside runLapseTicks, and cannot pass tradeMaxTicks without a close: at the limit it breaks, and that fighter's next landed blow is the close. Who it breaks for (section 9d): a lead of more than levelWithin takes it, at the limit or on the tick one appears after it; runs within levelWithin are a level trade, which goes on, and one still level at doubleTicks is the double hit. staggeredAddsRun: whether a blow landed on a staggered fighter adds to the run (false: a close does not start the next lead). closeGuardTicks: a fighter cannot be closed on again for this long after he recovers from a close; the rival's run still counts, and a run of runToClose closes on his first blow after it. heavy: damage, its ki, windupTicks then landTicks to contact; his line is free `recover` ticks after a heavy that lands, breaks a guard or ends his string, and recoverWhiff after one that meets nothing (the 76 ticks of the spec are its animation, whose follow-through plays only when nothing follows); held past the wind-up it waits for the release, fully charged at heldFullTicks of hold and let go by itself at heldMaxTicks, and lands heldLandTicks after the release; staggerTicks: a lone heavy that lands, and any heavy on a guard, staggers him in place; force: the launch force of an ender whose launch is earned. hitstop: ticks, by the blow's weight. Clocks: taps, the line, the string and the idle count run on S.tick (through a hit-stop); wind-ups, reels and holds are live ticks. shotHeavyMul: a heavy shot is worth its kind's damage times damageMul times this, as a heavy blow is (bolts keep their value). shooter: to the AI a rival is a shooter when he has fired in the last firedTicks and has landed no melee blow on it in the last noMeleeTicks; it then takes its level's vsShooter numbers (ai.json) perfectBlock.staggerTicks, riposteTicks, riposteReelTicks, reversal (section 9f): inside a brawl a perfect block turns the blow, closes the attacker's string, clears his run and staggers him in place for staggerTicks; the blocker's next attack pressed within riposteTicks is the riposte, which can't be blocked or dodged (a light is worth skillMul brawl lights and reels for riposteReelTicks; a heavy is a brawl heavy, and against a turned heavy or ender it separates them as an ender does). A reversal staggers the attacker for reversal.staggerTicks and its heavy lands for certain reversal.contactTicks after the press, in place. Neither ends the brawl; on the brink both count launch.json setup.weight.riposte. Control (slice C1; docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md sections 1 and 7): each stick moves the pair's centre at nudgeMul of his free-flight speed (times nudge.guard while he guards), through Controls' ramp (data/input/timing.json aim.nudgeStart and aim.nudgeTicks); the centre's speed changes by at most a full nudge over nudgeRampTicks; carryShare of the two velocities added as they meet carries on and fades over carryTicks; the pair never moves more than maxStepBh in a tick; a player's held stick moves the pair his way by nudge.floor of his own nudge at least, whatever the AI's stick, the carry or the old drift say (two players who oppose still cancel); a step may not bring its middle within nudge.clearBh of a standing building's box. Both sticks held within partDeg of straight away for partTicks end the brawl, free. The double hit: each lands one blow worth skillMul brawl lights, double.windupTicks after the trade reaches doubleTicks level, and both are thrown double.throwBh from the centre over double.throwTicks. The three strengths (slices C2a and C2t; brawl-second-pass.md sections 1 to 3 and 5b; docs/director/brawl-c2.md): every worth is in brawl lights (light.damage times damageMul). medium (Y): windupTicks live ticks, worth, ki, its flurry (presses within gap[1]; a blow is worth rate for each tick of its gap, from gap[0]), reelTicks, recover and recoverWhiff (his line after one that lands, and after one that misses), guardChipMul on a guard, reachBh past striking distance. heavy (B with no stance held): the same, with staggerTicks for a clean one and for a blocker, force for its launches; armour: a light does lightMul and changes nothing, a medium ends the wind-up before mediumUntilTicks, and on a lunge a shot of shotMediumPower counts as a medium and of shotHeavyPower as a heavy; charge: still down at fromTicks it charges (ki is the whole price), full at fullTicks, lands landTicks after the release and by itself at maxTicks, worth[0] to worth[1], reach up to reachBh, and the AI lets go within aiReleaseTicks of the flash. woundLandTicks: a wound press that arrives already wound (the Simple layout) lands this much later. burst: a light still down read.burstStart live ticks after its press throws blows landing at lands (live ticks from the press); the first is worth second, the rest rate for each tick of their gap; reelTicks; runHalves halves of a run point each; openTicks after the last. give: giving ground at bhPerSec (times his speed over speedRef when bySpeed), guard behind a guard, the winder follows at follow, the gap opens at most leashBh past striking distance; a press closes a gap at closeTicksPerBh ticks a body height, at most closeMaxTicks, and no fighter of a brawl moves more than closeMaxBh in a tick (closeSlackBh is kept back for other rules); lightReachBh: a light lands from this far past striking distance; edgeBh: the outermost part of a reach doesn't connect. launcher: in an opening (a flurry's close, a broken guard, a perfect block, a zip's tech counter: a stagger of minStagger or more) a B winds windupTicks, is worth worth, costs ki and always lands; it launches, at flightMul of a heavy's launch force, unless he was launched in the last restS seconds of fight time, and then it knocks him back. energy.reach: with the energy family held, bolt (contactTicks, worth, ki, reelTicks, runHalves, shot: the kind of data/fight/shots.json it is to the core) and blast (windupTicks, worth, ki, shot; it is an ender: with his run at enderRun or more as it lands a clean hit knocks back knockBh, as half a set-up when halfSetup, and thrown cold it is a medium that reels reelTicks); flashEveryTicks: one landing in this long may take the full flash. nudge.stagger: a staggered fighter keeps this share of his nudge. plannedHeavyDamage: the data heavy's damage that marks a planned strike outside a brawl as heavy-class.

cameraIntent._note: The camera-intent feed (sim/director/camintent.gd; docs/director/camera-intent.md): render-only cam_intent cues of what the director has decided ahead (a planned exchange's beats and climax, a brawl's close and launcher, the send's plan, a perfect block's read, the clinch's clock). enabled false: no cue. It writes cues only, so play is the same either way.

recoilFlip._note: Recoil flips (sim/director/recoil.gd; Game Design's rulings-2026-10-19.md 2a, fight-feel.md section 2). A dodge tap in the first windowTicks live ticks of a knock-back backflips him out of it: the slide ends where he is, and he is carried flipBh further back, bowed arcBh, over flipTicks, and lands set. His next blow within counterTicks of the landing is a counter-rush: an approach with no crouch, no return and no first-move lock, at counterRush's speed. Free: no ki, no cooldown. With no press, a knock-back on the ground over flourishOverBh ends in Animation's flourish (the recoil cue, text flourish). The AI flips on its level's brawl.recoil.flip share (ai.json), tapping aiTapTicks into the window, and follows with a counter-rush on brawl.recoil.counter of its flips, aiCounterTicks after the landing. enabled false: nothing runs and no cue is sent.

heavy._note: Game Design's 1a (rulings-2026-10-22): a tapped heavy that lands clean in a brawl recoils him bh body heights as a slide of ticks, in place of its stagger in place; it opens the flip's window, and with no flip he reels reelTicks at its end. Only with recoilFlip on.

freezeWindows._note: No window gets shorter for a freeze (Game Design's rulings-2026-10-19b.md 4c; sim/director/windows.gd), while Simulation's hit-stop by weight is on (data/fight/hitstop.json; off: nothing here runs). A window open as a hit-stop starts keeps its live ticks through it; one at least minLiveTicks long has at least that many live ticks after the freeze (a perfect block's on a pending strike, the chain window, the brawl's riposte and launcher windows). A brawl light's window is its own 2 ticks and is left as it is.

calmTurn._note: The calm-moment turn, the director's part (sim/director/calm.gd; docs/director/calm-turn.md; Game Design's rulings-2026-10-19b.md section 1 with 1e, and rulings-2026-10-22.md 5a; the EP's of 2026-10-22: no ring read on the swap tick, the warm rate at most 32; World's WorldEpoch). The ask: at a pausing form step (full or short; live is not one) the pivot is the pair's midpoint as the pause starts and one ring is warmed, only a bearing that keeps the ground rule there being taken; at a launch's send the pivot is predicted (between the rest and the launcher, on the side it was sent), a bearing preferred that keeps the rule at the predicted spread plus predictMargin (with none, the smallest), and World's smallest bearing's ring is warmed with it as the fallback. The pick is by what a turn brings into view (score by kind: a rival's home, a landmark, a city, a town, his own home). The host warms the columns over the ticks to the moment, warmCols to warmColsMax a frame (the calm_turn cue carries the rate); when that is not enough by the moment, the pick waits, warming, for a later one, and a new send or pause keeps a waiting pick whose pair keeps its ground rule (else cancels it and asks again). The hold: the warm read done; the ground under each fighter moved at most World's moveMax (his distance from the pivot times the sine of the angle) at the chosen angle or the fallback's, where they stand; no exchange, approach, beam clash, taunt, flip, counter-rush, waiting attack or open finisher; and a moment: the first formTicks live ticks after a pausing form step's pause, or a fighter at rest from a send within landedTicks with both down or set (under setSpeed units a second); and World's calm. enabled false (or World's turn off): nothing runs.

press._note: A player's attack press reacts on its own tick (Controls' T1; the EP's brief of 2026-10-22 after Performance's input-latency-2026-10-22.md, where a light first reacted 5 ticks late: the opening cooldown). Only a player's presses (the AI's are as before). skipOpenCool: his request is not held by the match's opening cooldown (SimCore.newMatch's 0.6 s) while no exchange has started this match; a cooldown after an exchange still holds it. ackQueued: a request still waiting after the drain is acknowledged on its press tick, the cue press_ack, text queued, source its cell, n the tick it is due when the wait is a cooldown (else -1), amount the ticks to it. capTicks and setPieceCapTicks (Game Design's 7a): after an exchange ends the cooldown holds a player's request at most capTicks, after a set piece's end setPieceCapTicks (a signature's exchange, a finisher, a template tagged with one of setPieceTags, a throw); it is kept and thrown at the cap. The AI keeps the whole cooldown. capTicks -1: off.

mash._note: A mash's later blows flow (sim/director/mash.gd; Game Design's rulings-2026-10-22.md 6 (b); Simulation's light_flow). A mash is a run of one fighter's mashed or burst blows (a brawl blow that names light_mash), each within flowGapTicks live ticks of his last; it starts again after that many without one. Its first blow keeps light_mash; each later one names light_flow, which holds no stop. Only while hit-stop by weight is on.

wallKick._note: The wall kick (sim/director/wallkick.gd; Game Design's rulings-2026-10-22.md 2b and 5c; fight-feel.md section 3), on a face that holds (World's wall slam). A dodge tap in the last beforeTicks live ticks before he meets it arms the kick; at the contact, if he meets it at minIntoWall units a second or more into it (below that is Combat's plant, not built), the kick replaces the slam's stagger: he takes damageMul of the slam, with no hold, rebound or stagger, and the rival's first move after a wall slam (brawl.firstMove) is void. He kicks off toward his stick at keep of his arrival speed (neutral or into the face: straight off it; the AI: at the rival), a push of pushTicks live ticks in which his presses wait, then he has control again in free flight at the push's speed. A push toward the rival (within towardDot of the way to him) makes his first blow within rushBlowTicks of its start a rush blow, as the recoil flip's counter-rush is (recoilFlip.counterRush's speed, no crouch, no return, no first-move lock); into open air, plain free flight. The AI kicks on its level's wallKick share (ai.json), never sooner than its reaction time after the send, and presses the rush blow on its brawl.recoil.counter share. enabled false: nothing runs and no cue is sent.

chase._note: The chase of a launch is the zip (sim/director/chase.gd; Game Design's rulings-2026-10-22.md 7c; brawl-second-pass.md section 16). A player presses X or Y with LT held while his own launch flies; the AI chases at a send of its own on its level's chaseShare (ai.json; times skyMul when the send goes up into open sky), no sooner than its reaction time. Either pays the zip's ki (the strike's or the heavy's); without it there is no chase. The chase is a rush at the body re-aimed each live tick at speedMul times his speed, never under minSpeed u/s. Within catchBh of him while he flies the zip's blow lands and sends him on (the launch planner from where he is, at sendForce, the chaser's stick its tilt); when his landing comes first it arrives at his landing, for the first move; at most maxTicks. enabled false: nothing runs.

grapple._note: The grapple's director side, slice G1 (sim/director/grapple.gd; Game Design's docs/design/grapple.md; docs/director/grapple-director.md). enabled: false, A in a brawl is as before (an empty press). catch: tell, the ticks from A's press in a brawl to its landing (a blow that lands on him in them stops it); tech, the caught fighter's A within this many ticks of the landing breaks it; whiffOpen, a catch out of reach leaves him open this long. clinch: max ticks from the tie-up; a pulse every `pulse` ticks; an A inside `window` of one claims it, sharp inside `sharp`; the grip runs from -grip to grip; leadGuard, the catcher's lead on a rival who guards, winds or charges; partBh, both part this far past striking distance at the time and the tech; pushBh and pushFirstMove, the push-off's parting and the pusher's first move; aiOffsets, the AI's pummels off the pulse (never sharp). throw: acrossBh, a throw across is a knock-back this long; upBh and upOpen, a throw up lifts him this far and he is open this long; bury, a throw down to the ground buries him this long (both openings). lockout: the ticks a grab is refused after each attempt, and for both after a clinch ends with nobody thrown; noRegrab: a thrown fighter can't be grabbed for this long. G2: when both pummel one pulse the one nearer it by the tick takes the step; clinch.timeFirstMove, the grip's leader's first move at the time (the brawl lets go; at even it goes on); throw.ai, the AI's throw weights: down and up (halved while it lacks the launcher's ki), across scaled by 1 + (-care) x careW x the people within popR body heights of where he would land (over the planet reference, WorldStructures.popNearRef). throw.worth: a throw lands worth this many brawl lights (a heavy), before what it hands the brawl (2026-10-18). Later slices add Game Design's vicious, damage, wear, lead and pin, brace, braceRest and carry.

zip._note: The zip, slice Z1 (sim/director/zip.gd; docs/design/melee-press-feel.md section 2c). LT with X (strike) or Y (heavy) in band: ki paid at the press; tellTicks of tell; inTicks (the range by distance) on the way in; reachBefore ticks in reach before his blow and reachAfter after it; outTicks on the way out, plus 1 for each out.bhPerTick body heights of path past out.freeBh, out.maxTicks at most. heldTicks: the button kept down this long past the tell is the held reading (a zip strike is then in reach heldReachBefore ticks before its blow). floor: no way in or out is under max(minTicks, the distance in bh over bhPerTick, rounded up) (Legal RL-076). exit: awayBh more with the stick straight away, capBh at most from the rival; a blocked point slides slideDeg at a time, probes at most, to a point clear by clearBh. bowBh: the bow of a way out that passes the rival (over him; under him with the stick down and room beneath) or clears the ground. towardDeg, awayDeg, exitSteps: Game Design's stick rules. mul, reel (a zip strike) and stagger (a zip heavy) by reading. counter: a tech strike pressed from techBefore ticks before the arrival, or a heavy landing from heavyBefore ticks before it, until his blow lands, cancels the blow; a tech counter staggers him staggerTicks and is worth a skill strike times mul. knockdownTicks: the drop when a shot hits him on the way out. dodgeConvertTicks: a face press this soon after LT's press takes the dodge back.
